messages:
maya: noticed a p99 spike in hosted-us-west around 13:12 UTC, p99 ~900ms (baseline ~150ms). p95 elevated too. Short chat requests are worst hit. Queue depth rose briefly.

sam: alerted. Any deploys or config changes around then? graphs? :eyes: 

maya: deploy-bot shows a runtime canary at 13:05 - experiment/kernel-selector canary (10%). pulling profiler now.

jin: quick profiler summary:
```
kernel_selector: preferred=fast_sparse_v1 -> now prefers dense_for_mixed
avg_inflight_batch: 6.1 -> 1.2
batch_fill_factor: 0.78 -> 0.25
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.76 -> 0.41
gpu_util_host_peek: 88% -> sustained 97% on noisy host
```
Looks like mixed-length pairing pushed many small requests onto dense kernels, causing kernel fallback and serialization.

tracy: did rate limits change? if ingress slowed but queue persisted that's classic backlog from reduced throughput.

maya: no rate-limit changes. logs show ingress spike ~13:08 (a few clients ramped), but backlog continued after spike subsided.

sam: backlog persistence => something lowered effective throughput. kernel-selector preferring dense paths for mixed batches could add per-request latency and reduce batching efficiency. Also kv cache hit drop will worsen latency for short chats.

ops-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T13:05Z -> eng-runtime: experiment/kernel-selector(canary=10%)

jin: confirmed canary was ~10% of pods. selector heuristic now biases for accuracy on mixed-length traffic which picked dense kernels even when short sequences dominated.

maya: propose immediate actions:
- rollback kernel-selector canary (fast)
- temporarily lower max concurrency on identified hosts to mitigate noisy-tenant saturation
- pin short-sequence models to fast_sparse_v1 for the next 24h
- add counters: per-tenant kernel_fallbacks + kv_cache_evictions

tracy: rollback first. we need tail down quickly.

sam: starting rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback started -> experiment/kernel-selector(canary) (13:22 UTC)

jin: post-rollback quick metrics: within ~2 minutes p99 dropped to ~170ms, kv_cache_hit_rate back to ~0.70, avg_inflight_batch ~5.6, batch_fill_factor returned to ~0.74. GPU host utilization normalized.

maya: good recovery. follow-ups: collect per-kernel latency histograms (next 24h), add synthetic mixed-length batch test to CI to ensure selector prefers fast_sparse for short-heavy workloads, and alert when batch_fill_factor < 0.4 for >2m in hosted.

sam: assigning follow-ups: @jin add histograms & test harness; @maya open alert PR and write rollback runbook; @tracy run noisy-neighbor audit for the 13:00-13:30 window.

tracy: will check tenant placement, noisy VM signals, and whether particular customers caused the short-request ramp. if recurring, consider stronger isolation for small-request-heavy tenants.

maya: thanks. will close thread after PRs + docs are in. :thumbsup:
